title: Ambarella (AMBA): The Memory Crunch Exposed a Business That Has Never Earned Its Stock Comp
description: Ambarella fell 40% this week after guiding next quarter 37% lower on the memory price spike. At $35.24 it is 46% below its 200-week line, yet even its record year did not cover $98M of stock comp. I call it a value trap, priced for a buyer that has not appeared.
verdict_label: Avoid — cheap against its line, still dear against its cash
selection_rationale: AMBA fell 40.2% after guiding Q4 revenue to $70-75M against about $112M expected, blaming the memory price spike, and now sits 46% below its 200-week line. It has a company-specific cause, years of filings and a live debate: temporary shock and takeover candidate, or a business whose economics never covered its stock comp. KYMR scored slightly higher on a Phase 2b win but has no product revenue to support the format; INSM is a merger-arb pin on Sanofi's bid; NTNX and ANF were smaller stories.
